title: Rust: Factory Pattern
description: Implement factory pattern for creating objects polymorphically.

steps.title: Simple Factory Function
steps.description: Define a `Shape` trait with `fn area(&self) -> f64`. Implement Circle, Rectangle, Triangle. Create a factory function `make_shape(kind: &str, params: Vec<f64>) -> Box<dyn Shape>`.

verification.failureMessage: Create a circle with radius 5 using the factory and print its area.

steps.title: Factory with Parameter Validation
steps.description: Make the factory return `Result<Box<dyn Shape>, String>`. Validate that the correct number of parameters is provided. Test with valid and invalid parameters.
hints: Circle needs 1 param, Rectangle needs 2, Triangle needs 2.
Handle both Ok and Err in main.

verification.failureMessage: Create valid shapes and handle invalid parameters.

steps.title: Registry-Based Factory
steps.description: Instead of hardcoded match arms, use a `HashMap<String, Box<dyn Fn(Vec<f64>) -> Box<dyn Shape>>>` as a registry where new shape types can be registered dynamically.
hints: `let mut registry: HashMap<String, Box<dyn Fn(Vec<f64>) -> Box<dyn Shape>>> = HashMap::new();`
New shape types can be added without changing the factory function.

verification.failureMessage: Register and create shapes using the registry.

steps.title: Abstract Factory
steps.description: Create an abstract factory: a `GUIFactory` trait with methods `create_button() -> Box<dyn Button>` and `create_checkbox() -> Box<dyn Checkbox>`. Implement `WindowsFactory` and `MacFactory`.

verification.failureMessage: Create UI widgets for both Windows and Mac factories.

steps.title: Factory Method
steps.description: Implement the Factory Method pattern: a `Document` trait with `fn create_row(&self) -> Box<dyn Row>`. Implement `CSVDocument` and `JSONDocument` that each create their own row type.
hints: The document defines which row type to create (Factory Method).

verification.failureMessage: Create CSV and JSON documents and print their rows.
